title: Minimum Distance Between Two Values
statement:
You are given an array `arr` of `n` integers and two **different** integers `x` and `y`. Each of `x` and `y` is guaranteed to appear in `arr` at least once.

The distance between an occurrence of `x` at index `i` and an occurrence of `y` at index `j` is `|i - j|`. Find the smallest such distance over all pairs of an occurrence of `x` and an occurrence of `y`.
input_format:
The first line contains an integer `n`.
The second line contains `n` space-separated integers: the array `arr`.
The third line contains two integers `x` and `y`.
output_format: Print a single integer: the minimum of `|i - j|` over all indices `i`, `j` with `arr[i] = x` and `arr[j] = y`.
constraints: Both x and y occur in arr at least once

examples.explanation: The value 3 is at indices 0 and 11; the value 6 is at indices 4, 6 and 7. The closest pairs are (0, 4) and (11, 7), both at distance 4.
Indices 0 and 1 hold 2 and 1, which are adjacent, so the distance is 1.
The only 1 is at index 0 and the only 3 is at index 6.

hints: Checking every pair of an x-position and a y-position is too slow when both values are frequent.
Scan left to right and remember the most recent index where you saw x and the most recent index where you saw y.
Whenever you see x, compare it with the last y seen (and the other way round). The best partner for an element on its left is always the nearest one.

import sys

data = sys.stdin.read().split()
n = int(data[0])
arr = [int(v) for v in data[1:1 + n]]
x, y = int(data[1 + n]), int(data[2 + n])
best = n
for i in range(n):
    for j in range(n):
        if arr[i] == x and arr[j] == y:
            best = min(best, abs(i - j))
print(best)
